authors: Eui-Soon Park, Bae-Hoon Kim, Pradeep Kumar, Kyle Tretina, Agnieszka Maminska, William M. Philbrick, ...
abstract: A study engineered mice lacking seven guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) to investigate their role in cytosolic LPS recognition. The findings reveal a hierarchical GBP network that controls key steps in the inflammasome pathway, protecting against Gram-negative sepsis.

abstract: Polymeric guanylate binding protein-1 (GBP1) directly binds to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) on gram-negative bacteria. This binding disrupts the bacterial cell envelope, leading to increased susceptibility to antibiotics and impaired function.

abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are interferon-induced proteins crucial for host defense against pathogens. They play multifaceted roles in immunity, impacting cellular processes and contributing to disease pathogenesis.

authors: Lucy Fry; Het Adhvaryu; Hayden Roys; Anne Bowlin; Gopinath Venugopal; Jordan T. Bird; Charity Washam...
abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (Gbps) are crucial for controlling *Leishmania major* infection. Gbps regulate inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and Arginase-1 (Arg-1) in myeloid cells, promoting parasite clearance and reducing disease severity. This function is independent of Gbps directly targeting the parasite.
